executive_summary.one_paragraph: COVE User Service is a reactive Spring Boot microservice deployed on AWS EKS that provides JWT-based authentication, user registration with admin-approval workflows, and role-based access control for the COVE platform. Primary users include end-users registering for accounts (CUSTOMER role) and administrators managing user onboarding, account activation, and role assignments (ADMIN role). The system integrates with external OneView API for project performance data, uses MySQL for persistence, and sends email notifications via Gmail SMTP. The architecture follows a layered pattern with reactive programming (Spring WebFlux), stateless JWT authentication, and comprehensive audit logging for compliance.

key_characteristics.characteristic: Reactive microservice architecture with Spring Boot 3.2.5 and WebFlux
JWT-based stateless authentication with short-lived access tokens (30 min) and long-lived refresh tokens (24 hours)
Admin-approval onboarding workflow with email notifications at each stage (pending, approved, rejected)
Role-based access control with CUSTOMER and ADMIN roles; admin endpoints protected via Spring Security
Comprehensive audit logging for all administrative actions (onboarding, account status, role changes)
AWS EKS deployment with automated CI/CD via AWS CodeBuild; Prometheus metrics for observability

drivers.rationale: JWT-based authentication with token revocation, BCrypt password hashing, role-based access control, and comprehensive audit logging are implemented to meet security and compliance requirements. However, critical security gaps exist (hardcoded credentials, missing SSL/TLS for database, no rate limiting).

Reactive programming with Spring WebFlux, stateless JWT authentication, and Kubernetes deployment with 2 replicas and resource limits support horizontal scaling. Service discovery via Eureka enables dynamic service registration.
Prometheus metrics exposed via Spring Actuator enable monitoring of application health, JVM metrics, and custom metrics. Kubernetes deployment includes Prometheus scrape annotations.
Automated CI/CD pipeline via AWS CodeBuild with Docker image build, ECR push, and EKS deployment reduces manual deployment effort. Kubernetes rollout restart ensures zero-downtime updates.

notable_patterns.description: Clear separation of concerns with Controller -> Service -> Repository layers. Each layer has distinct responsibilities and dependencies flow downward.
Spring WebFlux with Mono and Flux for non-blocking I/O. Reactive custom DAO (CustomerDaoImpl) for database queries.
Spring Data JPA repositories abstract database access with custom query methods and pagination support.
Data Transfer Objects (AuthUser, AuthenticationRequest, Token, SuccessResponse, etc.) separate API contracts from domain entities.
JWT authentication filter (JwtTokenAuthenticationFilter) intercepts requests to validate tokens before reaching controllers.

integration_architecture.summary: The system integrates with seven external touchpoints: OneView API (outbound REST for performance data), AWS RDS MySQL (outbound JDBC for persistence), Gmail SMTP (outbound SMTP for email notifications), Netflix Eureka (bidirectional REST for service discovery), Prometheus (inbound HTTP scrape for metrics), AWS ECR (outbound Docker Registry API for image storage), and AWS EKS (bidirectional Kubernetes API for orchestration). Authentication patterns vary: custom token for OneView, basic auth for MySQL and Gmail, unknown for infrastructure services. No explicit retry logic at application level; relies on library defaults. Idempotency is not enforced for write operations.

touchpoint_groups.source_ref: integration_catalog.json: AWS ECR, AWS EKS enrichments

data_architecture.summary: The system uses MySQL 8.0.33 on AWS RDS as the primary relational database with four tables: users (user entities with onboarding status and account activation), access_token (short-lived JWT tokens), refresh_token (long-lived JWT tokens), and action_history (audit log for admin actions). Data ownership is clear: User Management Context owns users table, Authentication & Authorization Context owns token tables, Audit & Compliance Context owns action_history table. Relationships are enforced via JPA annotations (one-to-many from users to tokens, logical association from users to action_history via email). No database migration tooling detected; schema evolution relies on JPA auto-DDL. No caching layer or data retention policies implemented.

persistence_and_flow_notes.note: User registration creates a UserEntity with pending_approval status and isActive=false. Admin approval updates onboardingStatus to approved and isActive=true.
Login generates new access and refresh tokens, revokes old tokens by setting revoked=true. Tokens are stored in database with expiration flags.

security_and_privacy_architecture.summary: The system implements JWT-based stateless authentication with short-lived access tokens (30 min) and long-lived refresh tokens (24 hours). Passwords are hashed with BCrypt before storage. Role-based access control (RBAC) protects admin endpoints (/api/v1/admin/**) with ADMIN role requirement. Tokens are stored in database with expiration and revocation flags. Audit logging records all admin actions with timestamps and attribution. However, critical security gaps exist: hardcoded credentials in source code (OneView API) and configuration files (database, SMTP), missing SSL/TLS for database connections, no rate limiting or account lockout for authentication endpoints, no multi-factor authentication (MFA), and no comprehensive audit logging for authentication events.

control_highlights.description: Access tokens (30 min) and refresh tokens (24 hours) are signed with HS256. Tokens are stored in database with revoked flag. Old tokens are revoked on login.
User passwords are hashed with BCrypt before storage. Plain text passwords are never stored or logged.
Admin endpoints require ADMIN role. JWT token filter validates role claims before allowing access.
All admin actions (onboarding status, account status, role changes) are logged in action_history table with admin email, user email, action details, and timestamps.
control_highlights.source_ref: security_privacy_assessment.json: sensitive_data_identification (Audit and Compliance Data); business_process_model.json: proc_admin_onboarding_approval

control_highlights.description: OneView API and Gmail SMTP integrations use HTTPS/SSL. Kubernetes service exposes port 80 internally (ClusterIP); external HTTPS termination assumed at ingress/load balancer.
control_highlights.source_ref: integration_catalog.json: OneView API, Gmail SMTP enrichments; repository_summary.json: kubernetes_configuration

business_alignment.summary: The software architecture directly supports six core business processes: User Registration (proc_user_registration), Admin Onboarding Approval (proc_admin_onboarding_approval), User Login (proc_user_login), Token Refresh (proc_token_refresh), Admin Account Management (proc_admin_account_management), and Admin Role Management (proc_admin_role_management). Each process is implemented via REST API endpoints, service layer orchestration, and database persistence. Email notifications keep users informed during onboarding. Audit logging ensures compliance and traceability for admin actions. The architecture enables controlled access to the COVE platform with admin oversight.
